threads.body: [General] This duplicates `DbServerTargetBuilder.isIpv4Literal` (lines 232–254). Keeping two copies means a future validation fix can make standalone IPv4 endpoints and IPv4-embedded IPv6 endpoints disagree; move the shared IPv4 parser here and have the builder delegate to it as well.

[General] This blacklist omits several URI reserved delimiters. For example, `isIpv6Literal("fe80::1%5Devil")` currently returns true even though `5D` encodes `]`, which can terminate the bracketed host after percent-decoding; `5B`, `21`, and `3B` are likewise accepted. Reject the complete RFC 3986 reserved set (while retaining the existing `\` and `%` safeguards) so the new validation fulfills its encoded-delimiter safety goal.

replies.body:
Addressed in a6f8aa730f4c47c75d1678eaf0d8522dc4a17dea.

Analysis: The existing check covered only part of the RFC 3986 reserved set. Decode the leading hexadecimal pair and reject every general delimiter and sub-delimiter, plus backslash and percent.

Upsides: Encoded zone identifiers can no longer introduce any URI reserved delimiter after decoding. Tests cover each newly rejected character.

Downsides: No material downside identified.
